subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Kitsune the Fox Spirit
description: A quick, practical guide to Kitsune the Fox Spirit.

hook.text: Japanese kitsune are fox spirits who can assume human form. The older the fox, the more tails and more power.

buildup.text: A nine-tailed kitsune is near-divine. Some serve the rice god Inari. Others seduce and destroy humans.

discovery.text: Kitsune wives appear in many tales—a beautiful woman reveals fox ears or a tail, and the marriage dissolves.

twist.text: The kitsune wife genuinely loves her human husband. Her exposure isn't deception unmasked—it's identity revealed.

climax.text: Kitsune blur the line between trick and truth. The disguise may be more real than the original form.

punchline.text: The mask became the face. Or was it always?

quiz.question: What indicates a kitsune's power in Japanese mythology?
